audit.title: Off-Chain Policy Execution

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong. Opens with a self-contained definition — "Off-chain policy execution lets you enforce compliance rules that depend on data or systems outside the blockchain." Each section leads with its answer. No action needed.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong hierarchy (1 H1, H2s, no level skips, 0 sections over 600 words). Weak spot: 0 tables — the managed-vs-custom distinction is the page's core decision and lives in prose/bullets, not an extractable table.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. 15 numerals but 0 with units, no version strings, no thresholds/latencies/limits. Good specific: "permits are single-use and do not expire." Missing quantitative detail on risk thresholds, rate/usage limits, Beta scope.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 11 internal links, well-chosen (reference contract, guides). 0 external — no link to TRM, DON docs, or Keystone Forwarder canonical definitions, which would raise attributability.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good. "The permit serves as cryptographic proof that the off-chain checks passed." Crisp and liftable. Permit and off-chain policy both defined near first use.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak per measured facts — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no `datePublished`/`dateModified` in head (only "Last Updated: 2026-07-17" in body). Head metadata not captured; CLI should pass raw `<head>` to confirm.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code blocks. Conceptual page, so partially N/A, but the Evaluation API call flow is described verbatim without a single request/response snippet an agent could adapt.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers what/why/how and both models. Missing troubleshooting and symptom-phrased entry points (e.g., the permit-revert case is buried in prose, not a heading).

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Clear and consistent overall. Minor: "off-chain" and "offchain" are both used, which can fragment entity resolution.

audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured conceptual page explaining ACE off-chain policy execution, with a strong lifted-answer intro and clear numbered flows for both the managed and custom models. Its single biggest strength is answer-first extractability; its biggest opportunity is a managed-vs-custom comparison table plus machine-readable metadata (no JSON-LD, missing canonical, dates only in body). The honest verdict: solid conceptual prose that an engine can quote, but under-instrumented for retrieval and thin on concrete numbers.

recommendations.title: Add a managed-vs-custom comparison table
recommendations.where: After the intro's two-bullet list, before "Why off-chain policies?"
recommendations.issue: The core choice is split across prose bullets: "Managed wallet risk screening (MVP)" vs "Custom offchain integrations."
recommendations.change: Add a table with rows: use case, who hosts infrastructure, availability (MVP/Beta), permit lifetime, setup path (link), example providers.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract *reasons* and build justified "which should I use" answers; the current bullets don't chunk as a decision unit.

recommendations.title: Add machine-readable metadata
recommendations.issue: Measured facts show 0 JSON-LD, canonical MISSING, no `dateModified` in head.
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified` (surface the body's 2026-07-17), canonical URL, and `inLanguage`.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and visible freshness raise parse-ability and E-E-A-T trust for agents.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-phrased heading for the permit-revert case
recommendations.issue: Key failure mode is buried: "will revert if the caller does not have a valid permit."
recommendations.change: Add an H3 like "Why does my protected function revert without a permit?" answering it in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by symptom/error; concept-titled prose loses that retrieval even when the answer is present.

recommendations.title: Inject concrete specifics
recommendations.where: "Managed wallet risk screening" and "Custom offchain integrations."
recommendations.issue: Qualitative-only: "risk thresholds," "usage limits," with 0 numerals carrying units.
recommendations.change: State permit properties explicitly (single-use, non-expiring in Beta), name the threshold types (global risk, unknown-risk, category-specific), and any known limits.
recommendations.why: Quantitative/specific claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal Evaluation API request example
recommendations.where: Step 1 of the managed flow ("calls the ACE Evaluation API with...").
recommendations.issue: The call is described in prose with named parameters but no snippet.
recommendations.change: Add a fenced, language-tagged example showing the request body (caller, target, function, chain, permit params) and the polled `status` values (`rejected`, `ready`).
recommendations.why: Copy-pasteable, complete snippets are directly liftable by coding agents.

recommendations.title: Add authoritative external links
recommendations.where: First mentions of "TRM Wallet Screening," "Keystone Forwarder," "Vault DON."
recommendations.issue: 0 external links; these entities are unlinked.
recommendations.change: Link each to its canonical source/definition.
recommendations.why: Inline authoritative references raise credibility and citation rate.

recommendations.title: Normalize "off-chain"/"offchain" spelling
recommendations.issue: Mixed spelling of the central term.
recommendations.change: Pick one form site-wide and apply consistently.
recommendations.why: Consistent naming aids entity resolution and reduces ambiguity.

antiPatterns: Two `(Image: Image)` placeholders with no alt text or caption — invisible to engines; add descriptive captions of the flow each diagram shows.
No stale-content or keyword-stuffing issues; prose is clean and non-promotional.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced in-page — good; confirm it lists this URL.
Site-level JSON-LD/canonical emission and freshness cadence are template concerns beyond this page.
Third-party citations (e.g., TRM docs linking back) are earned/off-page and not scored here.
